records.title: ROBERT tab
question_patterns: what is the ROBERT tab
where do I configure a model

user_guidance.purpose: Configure training and test data, choose the machine-learning task and workflow, and launch ROBERT.
when_to_use: Use this tab for model preparation, ROBERT execution, and the main EasyROB run controls.
prerequisites: A suitable CSV, with descriptors already present or SMILES available for optional AQME generation.
steps: Load the main CSV.
Choose target, prediction type, and workflow.
Press Run ROBERT.
user_guidance.result: The selected ROBERT stages run; Results and its child views become available when their corresponding artifacts exist.
next_steps: Monitor the console, then open Results and inspect its enabled Report, Predictions, Images, or Interactive plots views.
common_issues: Raw structures need AQME descriptors before they can serve as ROBERT model features.

records.title: AQME tab
question_patterns: what is the AQME tab
where do I set descriptor options

user_guidance.purpose: Configure advanced AQME options, including common-pattern atom selection for atom-specific descriptors and ChemDraw or SDF conversion tools.
when_to_use: Open this optional tab only when advanced AQME settings or atom-specific descriptors are needed.
prerequisites: Enable AQME Workflow and load a main CSV with valid SMILES only when these advanced options are needed.
steps: Inspect mapped atoms, Solvent, and Descriptor Level only when an advanced setting must change. Standard molecular descriptor generation does not require opening this tab.
user_guidance.result: The tab configures optional AQME details; standard descriptor generation and integrated ROBERT runs can proceed without visiting it.
next_steps: Use Run AQME for descriptor-only output, or Run ROBERT with Enable AQME Workflow for an integrated model run.
common_issues: There is no separate AQME CSV selector; AQME uses the main CSV loaded on ROBERT. Descriptor Level affects integrated Run ROBERT; standalone Run AQME generates all three descriptor levels.

records.title: Advanced Options tab
question_patterns: what is in Advanced Options
should I change ROBERT defaults
what is advaned options tab

user_guidance.purpose: Expose detailed ROBERT options grouped by workflow stage for users who need controlled departures from defaults.
when_to_use: Use Advanced Options only when the data, method, or diagnostic question gives a specific reason to tune a setting.
prerequisites: Understand which ROBERT stage consumes the option and how the change affects validation or reproducibility.
steps: Open the relevant GENERAL, CURATE, GENERATE, or PREDICT group and consult its help before editing.
user_guidance.result: The changed values are included in the next compatible ROBERT command.
next_steps: Return to ROBERT and run the selected workflow.
common_issues: Defaults are appropriate for typical runs; changing many options without a rationale can obscure failures.

records.title: GENERATE hyperoptimization settings
question_patterns: how do we use hyperoptimization in this process
how do I configure hyperoptimization
what are init_points and n_iter

user_guidance.purpose: Tune ROBERT's Bayesian hyperoptimization settings in the GENERATE group of Advanced Options.
when_to_use: Use these settings only when you have a reason to change the default search effort or expected improvement.
prerequisites: Valid descriptors, a target, and a compatible ROBERT GENERATE or Full Workflow run are required before hyperoptimization can evaluate models.
steps: Open Advanced Options and the GENERATE group.
Set init_points for the initial search points, n_iter for the optimization iterations, and expect_improv for the expected improvement criterion.
Run the selected ROBERT workflow and inspect the console and reports.
user_guidance.result: ROBERT uses the supplied GENERATE values when it performs its hyperoptimization process.
next_steps: Keep the defaults unless the experiment requires a controlled change and record the values for reproducibility.
common_issues: There is no separate Enable Hyper-optimization checkbox or algorithm selector in this GUI; do not infer one from backend or command-line documentation.

records.title: Results Report view
question_patterns: when does Reports become available
where is the ROBERT PDF
why is the Reports tab locked

user_guidance.purpose: Display the generated ROBERT report PDFs for the available No PFI and PFI model variants.
when_to_use: Open Results > Report after a workflow has created a matching ROBERT report file.
prerequisites: At least one report PDF for the selected model and variant.
steps: Open Results, choose Best models or a named model, then select Report and compare the No PFI and PFI PDFs with their validation evidence.
user_guidance.result: Best models shows the two GENERATE-selected model variants; selecting a named model shows that model's available variant PDFs from REPORT_models.
next_steps: Compare each report with the same model's Images, Predictions, and Interactive plots.
common_issues: Report remains disabled for a selection without matching PDFs. The two root-level report PDFs can be REPORT's best-scoring reports and need not match GENERATE's Best models selection.

records.title: Results Predictions view
question_patterns: when does Predictions become available
where can I see predicted values
why are all my predictions identical

user_guidance.purpose: Display external prediction tables in separate No PFI and PFI subtabs, with a model-specific score and diagnostics dashboard when its report is available.
when_to_use: Open Results > Predictions when prediction CSV files exist for the selected model; identical predictions can signal an uninformative model or incompatible inputs.
prerequisites: Discovered internal or external prediction CSV artifacts for the selected model and variant.
steps: Open Results, select Best models or a named model, then open Predictions and compare values and standard deviations across its available variants.
user_guidance.result: EasyROB presents generated prediction rows for inspection, sorting, and plotting, alongside diagnostics from the corresponding variant report.
next_steps: Interpret predictions with model validation, applicability, and uncertainty.
common_issues: The Predictions view stays disabled when no matching prediction CSV files are found for the selection. An external Test CSV is needed only for external predictions.

records.title: Check model tab
question_patterns: what does Check model do
how do I evaluate my own model
why is there only a No PFI report after Check model

user_guidance.purpose: Evaluate a supplied scikit-learn model or ROBERT's default MVL model without GENERATE's model search.
when_to_use: Use Check model when the model or its hyperparameters are already chosen and you want ROBERT's validation and report workflow.
prerequisites: Select a training CSV, target column, name column, prediction type, and optional external test CSV.
steps: Choose the model source, run EVALUATE, then inspect its No PFI PDF in Results > Report and any external prediction table in Results > Predictions.
user_guidance.result: EVALUATE runs validation and reporting for the supplied model and creates ROBERT_report_No_PFI.pdf; it does not generate a PFI variant.
next_steps: Judge Interpolation and, for regression, Boundary robustness using the validation evidence in the report.
common_issues: Predictions is available only when compatible external prediction CSV files were produced.

records.title: Results Images view
question_patterns: where are ROBERT plots
when does Images become available
where can I find generated plots

user_guidance.purpose: Browse figures generated by CURATE, GENERATE, VERIFY, PREDICT, and other completed workflow stages.
when_to_use: Open Results > Images after EasyROB detects figures for the selected run and model.
prerequisites: A completed stage that produced supported image files.
steps: Open Results, select Best models or a named model, choose Images and a stage group, then inspect, copy, save, or open a figure.
user_guidance.result: Generated plots are grouped by workflow stage in one viewer.
next_steps: Relate plots to the corresponding report and console evidence.
common_issues: The Images view is artifact-driven and remains disabled when no matching images are available.

records.title: Results Interactive plots view
question_patterns: where are the interactive plots
when does the Williams plot unlock
how do I choose a model in Results

user_guidance.purpose: Explore prediction and Williams applicability plots for the model variants selected in Results.
when_to_use: Open the view when its prediction CSV and plot data are available for the selected model.
prerequisites: Matching model prediction files and supported plot data.
steps: Open Results, choose Best models or a named model, then select Interactive plots and the available No PFI or PFI graph.
user_guidance.result: The graphs use the same model and variant selection as the Report, Predictions, and Images views.
next_steps: Compare points and applicability limits with the matching PDF and DAT metrics.
common_issues: A disabled Interactive plots button means no supported interactive plot data was detected for that selection.

records.title: MolSSI Databases tab
question_patterns: what is the MolSSI Databases tab
how do I use MolSSI descriptor data

user_guidance.purpose: Browse molecular descriptor libraries and download selected MolSSI data for an EasyROB workflow.
when_to_use: Use this tab when a suitable library can supply descriptors or an external comparison dataset.
prerequisites: Choose a relevant library and understand whether the downloaded table should be a main or test dataset.
steps: Browse the embedded database, select data, download it, and follow the resulting load or save message.
user_guidance.result: The data is saved; automatic suggestions may load a generated main CSV or populate the Test CSV, while ordinary downloads may require manual loading.
next_steps: Return to ROBERT and confirm which CSV slot contains the dataset.
common_issues: Do not assume every in-tab download is automatically loaded into the workflow.

records.title: Select Input CSV File
question_patterns: how do I load the main CSV
which file trains ROBERT

user_guidance.purpose: Load the primary table used for ROBERT training or for AQME structure-to-descriptor processing.
when_to_use: Select a main CSV before model-building workflows and before AQME runs that consume a SMILES table.
prerequisites: The file must be readable CSV data with the columns needed by the selected workflow.
steps: Choose Select Input CSV File and open the intended table, then review the populated column selectors.
user_guidance.result: EasyROB displays the filename, loads columns, refreshes relevant state, and offers SMILES context to AQME when enabled.
next_steps: Choose target, task type, and workflow or inspect AQME structure options.
common_issues: Loading the wrong table changes every downstream selector, so verify the filename before running.

records.title: Select External Test CSV File (optional)
question_patterns: is the test CSV optional
where do I load new prediction rows

user_guidance.purpose: Select external rows for prediction or evaluation without replacing the main training CSV.
when_to_use: The test CSV is optional for model training but required for an external PREDICT workflow.
prerequisites: Use compatible descriptors, or ID and SMILES columns when the trained model used AQME descriptor generation.
steps: Choose the optional Test CSV and confirm that its descriptor strategy matches the trained model.
user_guidance.result: EasyROB stores the external path and can enable Predictions after compatible prediction files are generated.
next_steps: Choose PREDICT and run ROBERT.
common_issues: A test table with different descriptor columns cannot be substituted for the trained model inputs.

records.title: Select Target Column (y)
question_patterns: where do I select y
which property should ROBERT predict

user_guidance.purpose: Choose the main CSV column containing the property that ROBERT should learn and predict.
when_to_use: Set the target after the main CSV columns have loaded and before running model-building stages.
prerequisites: The chosen column must represent the intended measured outcome, not a name, SMILES, or unrelated metadata field.
steps: Open Select Target Column (y), choose the response column, and verify its values.
user_guidance.result: ROBERT uses the selected column as the modelling target throughout compatible stages.
next_steps: Set Prediction Type to match continuous values or classes.
common_issues: An incorrect target can produce a technically successful model for the wrong question.

records.title: Prediction Type
question_patterns: where do I choose regression
how do I select classification

user_guidance.purpose: Select Regression for a continuous target or Classification for discrete target classes.
when_to_use: Choose the task type for every new ROBERT configuration.
prerequisites: Understand whether numerical distance between target values is meaningful or whether values are labels.
steps: Open Prediction Type and select Regression or Classification to match the target.
user_guidance.result: ROBERT uses task-appropriate models, metrics, and validation logic.
next_steps: Select the workflow and review any advanced options.
common_issues: A column containing numbers can still represent classes, so choose based on meaning rather than storage type.

records.title: ROBERT workflow selector
question_patterns: which ROBERT workflow should I choose
where do I select PREDICT

user_guidance.purpose: Choose Full Workflow or one ROBERT stage: CURATE, GENERATE, PREDICT, VERIFY, or REPORT.
when_to_use: Use Full Workflow for a new complete run and individual stages when valid prior outputs already exist or a focused rerun is intended.
prerequisites: Know which input and previous-stage artifacts the chosen stage requires.
steps: Select the workflow, review its required CSV and folders, then press Run ROBERT.
user_guidance.result: Only the selected stage sequence is included in the ROBERT command.
next_steps: Monitor the console and inspect the artifacts produced by that stage.
common_issues: PREDICT needs a test CSV and trained model, while Full Workflow needs the training main CSV.

records.title: Enable AQME Workflow
question_patterns: what does Enable AQME Workflow do
how do I unlock AQME

user_guidance.purpose: Include AQME descriptor generation in a ROBERT run when the main CSV contains SMILES, while also unlocking the optional AQME tab.
when_to_use: Check it when the main CSV has structures such as SMILES and descriptors must be generated.
prerequisites: Load the main CSV first so EasyROB can rebuild the common SMILES context.
steps: Check Enable AQME Workflow on the ROBERT tab, complete the normal ROBERT model settings, and press Run ROBERT. Open AQME only if advanced options are needed.
user_guidance.result: When Run ROBERT starts, EasyROB generates molecular descriptors from the SMILES data and uses them in the selected ROBERT workflow. The checkbox also unlocks the optional AQME tab.
next_steps: Use Run AQME instead only when descriptor CSV files are the final goal without a model run.
common_issues: The checkbox does not enable Run AQME by itself. Leave it unchecked when a valid descriptor CSV is already ready for ROBERT.

records.title: Run ROBERT
question_patterns: how do I start ROBERT
what happens when I press Run ROBERT

user_guidance.purpose: Validate the current ROBERT configuration and launch the selected machine-learning stage or Full Workflow.
when_to_use: Press Run ROBERT after all required inputs and workflow choices are ready.
prerequisites: Main CSV, target, prediction type, and workflow are required as applicable; PREDICT also needs external data and a model.
steps: Review the configuration, press Run ROBERT, respond to any preflight prompt, and watch the console.
user_guidance.result: EasyROB starts the configured ROBERT job, disables conflicting run controls, and enables Stop while it runs.
next_steps: Inspect the tracked popup and output tabs after completion.
common_issues: A preflight message identifies missing input instead of starting an incomplete command.

records.title: Run AQME (descriptor generation)
question_patterns: how do I generate descriptors only
what does Run AQME start

user_guidance.purpose: Start AQME descriptor generation independently of ROBERT model training.
when_to_use: Use Run AQME when the immediate goal is to create descriptor CSV files from structures.
prerequisites: Load the main CSV with valid SMILES and review any AQME descriptor or atom settings.
steps: Press Run AQME (descriptor generation), confirm any descriptor notice, and follow progress in the console.
user_guidance.result: Standalone Run AQME generates denovo, interpret, and full descriptor tables regardless of Descriptor Level while both run controls are disabled and Stop is enabled.
next_steps: Load the chosen descriptor CSV into ROBERT when model building is needed.
common_issues: The button is separate from Enable AQME Workflow, and Descriptor Level applies to integrated Run ROBERT rather than this standalone action.

records.title: Stop
question_patterns: how do I stop a run
does Stop interrupt AQME

user_guidance.purpose: Request asynchronous termination of the active ROBERT or AQME worker after user confirmation.
when_to_use: Use Stop when the current job should not continue, such as after recognizing a wrong configuration.
prerequisites: A workflow must be running; Stop is disabled while EasyROB is idle.
steps: Press Stop, confirm the interruption, and wait for worker cleanup rather than closing files manually.
user_guidance.result: EasyROB requests termination, disables Stop during cleanup, and restores run controls when the worker finishes.
next_steps: Read the console, correct the configuration, and start a new run if needed.
common_issues: The console currently may say Stopping ROBERT even when the active worker is AQME.

records.title: Clear selected test CSV file
question_patterns: how do I clear the test CSV
does the X delete my test file

user_guidance.purpose: Remove the currently selected external Test CSV from the active EasyROB configuration.
when_to_use: Use the visible X when the external data should no longer participate in the next run.
prerequisites: A Test CSV selection is present; the clear button is hidden otherwise.
steps: Press the X with tooltip Clear selected test CSV file and verify that the selection disappears.
user_guidance.result: EasyROB clears the stored test path and rebuilds train-only AQME context; it does not delete the disk file or clear detected Results views.
next_steps: Select another Test CSV or continue without external prediction data.
common_issues: Old prediction artifacts may still exist even after the current Test CSV selection is cleared.

records.title: Tutorial
question_patterns: where are EasyROB tutorials
how do I open a workflow guide

user_guidance.purpose: Open task-oriented EasyROB tutorials with practical steps and screenshots for common workflows.
when_to_use: Use Tutorial when you want a guided sequence for a concrete task rather than detailed parameter reference.
prerequisites: Choose the tutorial closest to the intended starting data and outcome.
steps: Press Tutorial and select Overview, From CSV, From ChemDraw, Generate Descriptors, or New Predictions.
user_guidance.result: A Workflow Tutorial window presents the packaged click-by-click guide.
next_steps: Follow the selected guide, then use Documentation for deeper reference.
common_issues: A tutorial describes one supported path and does not replace checking the current file contents.

records.title: Documentation
question_patterns: where is EasyROB documentation
how do I read parameter details

user_guidance.purpose: Open deeper ROBERT, AQME, or EasyROB reference material for concepts, modules, and parameters.
when_to_use: Use Documentation when a tutorial is not detailed enough or an advanced option needs authoritative context.
prerequisites: Know which program, module, or visible option requires explanation.
steps: Press Documentation and navigate to the relevant ROBERT or AQME topic.
user_guidance.result: Reference information supplements the task-oriented Tutorial guides.
next_steps: Return to the GUI and apply only the settings needed for the workflow.
common_issues: Upstream documentation may describe command-line capabilities that are not exposed as EasyROB controls.

records.title: robBOT
question_patterns: how do I open robBOT
what can robBOT explain

user_guidance.purpose: Open the floating robBOT window for questions about GUI controls, workflows, outputs, warnings, and current tracked context.
when_to_use: Use robBOT when you need concise help tied to EasyROB rather than general chemistry or programming advice.
prerequisites: Choose an answer mode in Settings; Local AI and Cloud AI have additional model or provider requirements.
steps: Press robBOT, open Settings if needed, type a focused question, and press Send.
user_guidance.result: The robBOT Chat tab displays an answer using the selected mode and available EasyROB context.
next_steps: Apply the suggested check and confirm it against the popup, console, or documentation.
common_issues: Only tracked popups and a bounded console tail are available as current context.

records.title: robBOT Mode
question_patterns: which robBOT mode should I use
what is Heuristic mode

user_guidance.purpose: Choose how robBOT answers: deterministic Heuristic help, packaged Local AI, or an external Cloud AI provider.
when_to_use: Use Heuristic for stable rule-based guidance, Local AI for offline model answers, or Cloud AI when a configured provider is appropriate.
prerequisites: Local AI needs a downloaded and loaded model; Cloud AI needs a selected provider and API key.
steps: Open robBOT Settings and choose Local AI, Cloud AI, or Heuristic in Mode.
user_guidance.result: The robBOT title and enabled settings reflect the active answer mode.
next_steps: Prepare the local model or provider if required, then send a focused question.
common_issues: Changing modes does not repair missing model files or an invalid cloud credential.

records.title: robBOT Provider
question_patterns: how do I choose a cloud provider
why is Provider disabled

user_guidance.purpose: Select the external service used when robBOT Mode is Cloud AI and associate the request with that provider's API key.
when_to_use: Use Provider only for Cloud AI; Groq is the current default choice, with other supported providers available.
prerequisites: An account and valid API key for the selected provider, subject to that provider's access and billing rules.
steps: Choose Cloud AI, select Provider, enter the matching API key, and optionally save it locally.
user_guidance.result: Cloud questions are routed to the selected provider rather than Local AI or Heuristic logic.
next_steps: Press Send and review any provider error without exposing the key.
common_issues: A key from one provider does not authenticate another, and Provider is disabled outside Cloud AI mode.

records.title: robBOT Send
question_patterns: how do I ask robBOT
why is Send disabled

user_guidance.purpose: Submit the typed EasyROB question to the active robBOT answer mode.
when_to_use: Press Send after entering one focused question and preparing any required local model or cloud credential.
prerequisites: Non-empty question text and an available answer path for the selected mode.
steps: Describe the visible control, workflow, output, warning, or failure and press Send.
user_guidance.result: Input and settings are temporarily disabled while the reply is produced, then the answer appears in Chat.
next_steps: Apply the answer to the GUI and verify it against concrete popup, console, or report evidence.
common_issues: Broad questions without the relevant error or workflow state produce less specific guidance.

records.title: robBOT Clear
question_patterns: what does robBOT Clear remove
how do I reset the conversation

user_guidance.purpose: Remove the visible robBOT conversation and the retained dialog history used as conversation context.
when_to_use: Use Clear before starting an unrelated question or when previous discussion should no longer appear.
prerequisites: The action is available when robBOT is not busy answering.
steps: Press Clear in the robBOT window and confirm that the Chat history is empty.
user_guidance.result: The visible messages and retained history are cleared; packaged knowledge, GUI files, and API settings remain.
next_steps: Ask the new question with any relevant popup or console evidence.
common_issues: Clear does not erase workflow outputs or change the selected robBOT mode.

records.title: Prepare Local AI model
question_patterns: how do I load Local AI
why does robBOT say Download model

user_guidance.purpose: Download the packaged Local AI model when absent and load it into memory for offline robBOT answers.
when_to_use: Use this action after selecting Local AI when the status is not Model ready.
prerequisites: Allow the initial download when needed, ensure sufficient local storage, and wait for preparation to finish.
steps: Press Download model or Load model, confirm preparation, and wait until the status reports Ready.
user_guidance.result: The button progresses through preparing states and Local AI becomes available without a cloud API key.
next_steps: Return to Chat and press Send.
common_issues: Declining or failing preparation falls back to Heuristic help rather than leaving robBOT unusable.

records.title: AQME input from the main CSV
question_patterns: where do I load AQME input
is there an AQME file selector

user_guidance.purpose: Use the main CSV selected on ROBERT as AQME structure input when it contains a valid SMILES column.
when_to_use: Use this path for descriptor generation from a prepared CSV rather than from ChemDraw or SDF conversion.
prerequisites: Load the CSV with Select Input CSV File and enable the AQME tab if its options are needed.
steps: Load the main CSV, open AQME, and confirm that the molecule viewer detects the expected common pattern.
user_guidance.result: AQME receives train and optional test SMILES from the shared GUI state; there is no separate AQME file selector.
next_steps: Standalone Run AQME generates all three descriptor tables regardless of Descriptor Level; review that selector only for integrated Run ROBERT, plus any relevant solvent or atom mapping settings.
common_issues: A CSV without a SMILES column is valid for descriptor-based ROBERT but cannot drive structure-based AQME generation.

records.title: Select atoms in the molecule viewer
question_patterns: where is Map atoms
how do I choose atomic descriptors

user_guidance.purpose: Choose common-pattern atoms interactively for consistent atom-specific descriptor generation.
when_to_use: Use molecule-viewer selection when atomic descriptors are needed and the intended atom roles are unambiguous.
prerequisites: A main CSV with valid SMILES and a displayed common SMARTS pattern.
steps: Click the intended atoms in the molecule viewer and inspect their highlighted or numbered mapping.
user_guidance.result: Mapped SMILES are regenerated in memory for the selected atoms; there is no Map atoms button.
next_steps: Resolve metal or multiple-match warnings, then run AQME.
common_issues: Do not guess among several equivalent-looking matches; omit atomic descriptors if mapping is uncertain.

records.title: Generate CSV from ChemDraw Files or SDF file
question_patterns: how do I load ChemDraw structures
can EasyROB open an SDF file

user_guidance.purpose: Convert supported ChemDraw CDXML or SDF structures into a CSV table that EasyROB can use.
when_to_use: Use this action when the workflow starts from drawn structures rather than an existing CSV.
prerequisites: Save correct structures as CDXML or SDF; CDX is not supported, and target values still need to be supplied for supervised modelling.
steps: Open the converter, select the file, complete code_name and target data, and choose Save as CSV.
user_guidance.result: EasyROB saves the CSV and automatically loads it as the main input; ChemDraw feeds structures, not ready descriptors.
next_steps: Configure AQME descriptors, then return to ROBERT for model setup.
common_issues: Incorrect drawings, empty SMILES, or a nonnumeric target can block conversion.

records.title: Console output
question_patterns: what does the console show
where can I find the failure detail

user_guidance.purpose: Show read-only ROBERT or AQME progress, warnings, standard output, and concrete error details for the current run.
when_to_use: Read the console while a job runs and whenever a popup gives only a short summary.
prerequisites: Start a workflow; the console is cleared at the beginning of each new run.
steps: Follow the newest messages and copy the relevant failure lines before starting another job.
user_guidance.result: The console provides the detailed evidence needed to identify the stage and cause of a failure.
next_steps: Ask robBOT with the popup and recent console tail or consult the relevant documentation.
common_issues: Only the latest bounded console tail is supplied to robBOT, so preserve older details separately if needed.

records.title: Tracked popup message
question_patterns: what does this popup mean
can robBOT see the warning

user_guidance.purpose: Present the immediate user-facing event, such as missing setup, descriptor choice, completion, or a summarized failure.
when_to_use: Read the full title and message before dismissing a workflow popup.
prerequisites: The message must be routed through EasyROB's tracked popup path to remain available to robBOT.
steps: Note the popup wording, then inspect the console for supporting details.
user_guidance.result: An active or recently closed tracked popup can inform robBOT for a short period.
next_steps: Correct the stated prerequisite or use the console evidence to diagnose the failure.
common_issues: Not every QMessageBox is tracked, and old popup context expires rather than remaining indefinitely.

records.title: Workflow running state
question_patterns: how do I know a workflow is running
why are run buttons disabled

user_guidance.purpose: Prevent conflicting launches while a managed ROBERT or AQME worker is active and expose the safe interruption control.
when_to_use: Use this state to distinguish an active job from an idle interface.
prerequisites: A worker starts after successful preflight validation.
steps: Observe that Run ROBERT and Run AQME are disabled while Stop is enabled, and follow progress in the console.
user_guidance.result: Conflicting run actions remain unavailable until completion or cleanup, then both run buttons return and Stop is disabled.
next_steps: Wait for completion or press Stop and confirm if the job must end.
common_issues: Closing the window is not a substitute for waiting for asynchronous worker shutdown.

records.title: Start from a CSV
question_patterns: how do I start from a CSV
what CSV columns does EasyROB need

user_guidance.purpose: Configure an EasyROB modelling run from a CSV that contains descriptors directly or SMILES for optional AQME generation.
when_to_use: Use this workflow for a prepared table with identifiers, a target, and either descriptor columns or structures.
prerequisites: Check column names and values, decide the target and task type, and know whether AQME is needed.
steps: Load the main CSV.
Select target, prediction type, and name column.
Enable AQME only for structure-based descriptors.
Run ROBERT.
user_guidance.result: EasyROB runs the configured descriptor and model stages and enables Results views backed by generated files.
next_steps: Inspect the report and validation, then use a Test CSV for new predictions if needed.
common_issues: Do not enable AQME for an already valid descriptor table without a specific reason.

records.title: Start from ChemDraw or SDF
question_patterns: how do I start from ChemDraw
workflow from SDF to ROBERT

user_guidance.purpose: Convert ChemDraw CDXML or SDF structures into a CSV, generate descriptors, and continue to ROBERT model building.
when_to_use: Use this path when molecular drawings or an SDF are the starting material and no modelling table exists yet.
prerequisites: Correct structures plus code names and target values for supervised modelling; CDX files are unsupported.
steps: Enable AQME.
Generate CSV from ChemDraw Files or SDF file.
Complete and save the table.
Generate descriptors and press Run ROBERT.
user_guidance.result: The saved CSV becomes the main input, AQME derives descriptors, and ROBERT can train from the resulting table.
next_steps: Inspect Results > Report and Images, then add external prediction data when appropriate.
common_issues: ChemDraw supplies structures rather than descriptors, so successful conversion is not the end of model preparation.

records.title: Generate descriptor CSV files
question_patterns: how do I generate descriptors
what files does Run AQME create

user_guidance.purpose: Generate denovo, interpret, and full molecular descriptor tables from a main CSV containing SMILES.
when_to_use: Use descriptor-only generation when a table is needed before ROBERT or for another analysis.
prerequisites: Valid SMILES and any justified QDESCP descriptor, solvent, or mapped-atom settings.
steps: Load the main CSV.
Review relevant AQME settings while noting that Descriptor Level does not control standalone output.
Press Run AQME.
Wait for the descriptor completion message.
user_guidance.result: Standalone Run AQME writes denovo, interpret, and full descriptor CSV files regardless of Descriptor Level, without training a ROBERT model.
next_steps: Inspect the tables and load the chosen one on ROBERT when model building is intended.
common_issues: Add a target column before supervised ROBERT training if the descriptor output does not contain one.

records.title: Generate new predictions
question_patterns: how do I predict new candidates
workflow for a new Test CSV

user_guidance.purpose: Use an existing trained ROBERT model to predict compatible new candidate rows from a Test CSV.
when_to_use: Use this workflow after model generation when external candidates need predicted target values.
prerequisites: Keep the trained model folder available and prepare a Test CSV with matching descriptors or matching AQME-compatible structures.
steps: Select the Test CSV.
Choose PREDICT.
Press Run ROBERT.
Choose the descriptor strategy used during training.
user_guidance.result: ROBERT writes prediction tables and enables Predictions when the output files are discovered.
next_steps: Inspect values, uncertainty, and applicability in Predictions and the original report.
common_issues: Selecting Full Workflow with only a Test CSV does not replace the required training input.

records.title: Use MolSSI descriptor data
question_patterns: how do I use a MolSSI dataset
where does a MolSSI download go

user_guidance.purpose: Obtain a MolSSI descriptor library table and place it in the correct EasyROB main or external test role.
when_to_use: Use this workflow when a relevant functional-group library supplies descriptors or comparison molecules.
prerequisites: Choose the library and decide whether it is training input, a generated enriched main table, or external test data.
steps: Browse MolSSI Databases.
Download or accept the relevant suggestion.
Confirm which CSV slot was populated or load the saved file manually.
user_guidance.result: Conditional automatic flows load a generated main or Test CSV, while ordinary downloads remain saved for manual selection.
next_steps: Verify the selected path on ROBERT and configure the intended model or prediction workflow.
common_issues: A successful download message does not guarantee that every download was automatically loaded.

records.title: Inspect ROBERT results
question_patterns: how do I inspect results
which result tab should I use
where can I find generated plots

user_guidance.purpose: Combine the PDF report, stage figures, and external prediction tables instead of judging a workflow from one output.
when_to_use: Use this review after a ROBERT run has created result artifacts.
prerequisites: Open Results after output for this run is detected; each child view unlocks according to its files for the selected model.
steps: Choose Best models or a named model in Results.
Read Report for both available No PFI and PFI PDFs.
Inspect Images and Interactive plots for matching figures.
Use Predictions for matching internal or external CSVs.
user_guidance.result: The four views share the model selection and present matching model, validation, visualization, and inference evidence.
next_steps: Resolve warnings or data limitations before relying on the model.
common_issues: A disabled Results child view means its matching artifact was not produced or discovered for the selected model.

records.title: Diagnose a failed workflow
question_patterns: why did my workflow fail
how do I diagnose an EasyROB error
what should I check after a failed run

user_guidance.purpose: Identify a failed stage using the immediate popup, concrete console tail, current run state, and relevant prerequisite guidance.
when_to_use: Use this workflow when a run does not start, stops early, or finishes without the expected artifact.
prerequisites: Preserve the exact popup wording and newest console lines before launching another run.
steps: Read the popup.
Locate the first relevant console error.
Check required inputs and stage folders.
Ask robBOT a focused question with that evidence.
user_guidance.result: The failure is narrowed to a missing prerequisite, incompatible data, unavailable artifact, or execution error.
next_steps: Correct one concrete cause and rerun the smallest appropriate stage.
common_issues: Do not rely only on the final exception line when earlier console messages identify the actual input problem.

records.title: EasyROB overview tutorial
question_patterns: where is the EasyROB overview
which tabs are explained in the tutorial

user_guidance.purpose: Introduce the complementary AQME descriptor and ROBERT modelling roles, main controls, tabs, and output views.
when_to_use: Start here when EasyROB is new or when you need to understand how the major tabs connect.
prerequisites: No workflow output is required; knowing whether the starting data contains descriptors or structures is helpful.
steps: Open Tutorial.
Choose Overview.
Follow the packaged overview.md click-by-click guide and screenshots.
user_guidance.result: You can identify the setup, AQME, advanced, MolSSI, report, image, and prediction areas and their enabling conditions.
next_steps: Continue with the CSV, ChemDraw, descriptor, or prediction tutorial that matches the task.
common_issues: The overview explains navigation but does not replace checking a specific file's required columns.

records.title: From CSV tutorial
question_patterns: where is the CSV tutorial
how do I build a model from CSV

user_guidance.purpose: Show how to prepare and load a CSV, configure target and task type, optionally generate descriptors from SMILES, and run ROBERT.
when_to_use: Use this tutorial when the workflow starts from a spreadsheet or CSV table.
prerequisites: Prepare unique identifiers, a target, and either descriptor columns or a valid SMILES column.
steps: Open Tutorial.
Choose From CSV.
Follow csv.md for file preparation, GUI selection, AQME options, and Run ROBERT.
user_guidance.result: The workflow creates model outputs and enables available Results views after a successful run.
next_steps: Read the report and use the predictions tutorial for a later external test set.
common_issues: AQME can be skipped when descriptors are already included in the CSV.

records.title: From ChemDraw tutorial
question_patterns: where is the ChemDraw tutorial
how do drawings become a ROBERT model

user_guidance.purpose: Guide conversion of ChemDraw CDXML structures into a named, targeted CSV and continue through descriptors to ROBERT.
when_to_use: Use this tutorial when the starting molecules are drawn structures rather than a ready table.
prerequisites: Correct CDXML structures and the target values needed for supervised modelling.
steps: Open Tutorial.
Choose From ChemDraw.
Follow chemdraw.md through conversion, table completion, descriptor generation, and Run ROBERT.
user_guidance.result: The saved CSV is loaded as main input and can feed AQME and ROBERT.
next_steps: Use Results > Report and Images to inspect the completed workflow.
common_issues: CDX is unsupported, and ChemDraw files contain structures rather than model-ready descriptors.

records.title: Generate Descriptors tutorial
question_patterns: where is the descriptor tutorial
how do I run AQME without ROBERT

user_guidance.purpose: Show how to run AQME descriptor generation from a SMILES CSV without training a ROBERT model in the same job.
when_to_use: Use this tutorial when descriptor files are the immediate deliverable or must be reviewed before modelling.
prerequisites: A CSV containing valid SMILES and any intended atomic descriptor configuration.
steps: Open Tutorial.
Choose Generate Descriptors.
Follow descriptors.md to load input, press Run AQME, and locate the three outputs.
user_guidance.result: AQME creates denovo, interpret, and full descriptor CSV files.
next_steps: Inspect a descriptor table and add or confirm a target before loading it into ROBERT.
common_issues: Atomic descriptors require mapped atoms; molecular descriptors can be generated without atom selection.

records.title: New Predictions tutorial
question_patterns: where is the predictions tutorial
how do I predict new molecules

user_guidance.purpose: Guide prediction of new candidates with an existing ROBERT model and a compatible external Test CSV.
when_to_use: Use this tutorial after model training when new rows need predictions rather than model rebuilding.
prerequisites: Keep the trained model directory and prepare compatible descriptors or ID plus SMILES for the matching AQME strategy.
steps: Open Tutorial.
Choose New Predictions.
Follow predictions.md to select Test CSV, choose PREDICT, run ROBERT, and answer the descriptor prompt.
user_guidance.result: Prediction files are generated and the Results > Predictions view becomes available.
next_steps: Inspect predicted values and uncertainty alongside the original model report.
common_issues: The Test CSV must match how descriptors were supplied during model training.
